h1: Citizens National Bank of Meridian SBA loans (MS)
lede: The Citizens National Bank of Meridian is a long-established Mississippi community bank that lends to local businesses, including through SBA programs.
about: The Citizens National Bank of Meridian is a Mississippi-chartered community bank based in Meridian, in the east-central part of the state. It is one of the older independent banks in Mississippi and has stayed locally owned rather than selling to a regional or national holding company. That matters for business owners, because loan decisions are made by people who know the local economy.

The bank's home market is Lauderdale County and the surrounding east Mississippi counties, and over time it has added offices in other Mississippi markets. It offers the usual mix of deposit accounts, treasury services and commercial lending. Business borrowers tend to be owner-operated companies: medical and professional practices, contractors, retailers, timber and agriculture-related firms, and service businesses.

Because it is a full-service commercial bank, Citizens National handles conventional loans as well as government-guaranteed lending. SBA loans give it a way to say yes to deals that fall a little short of conventional standards, such as a thin down payment, a younger business, or collateral that does not fully cover the loan.
sba_fit: A Meridian-area owner would most likely come to Citizens National for a 7(a) loan to buy an existing local business, refinance expensive debt, or fund equipment and working capital. For an owner-occupied building, the bank can act as the first-lien lender in a 504 deal alongside a Mississippi CDC, which keeps the down payment near 10%. A relationship-driven bank like this usually wants your deposit accounts too, so expect the conversation to cover operating accounts and treasury services, not just the loan.

about: Bar Harbor Bank & Trust is the bank subsidiary of Bar Harbor Bankshares, a publicly traded holding company. For most of its history it served coastal Maine communities, where seasonal tourism, fishing, boatbuilding and hospitality shape the local economy.

The bank's footprint changed in 2017 when Bar Harbor Bankshares acquired Lake Sunapee Bank Group, the parent of Lake Sunapee Bank in New Hampshire. That deal added branches in New Hampshire and Vermont, and the Lake Sunapee branches were folded into the Bar Harbor name. Today the bank operates across all three northern New England states.

Business customers include hotels and inns, restaurants, marine businesses, contractors, healthcare practices and other owner-managed companies. The bank offers commercial real estate, equipment and working capital loans alongside cash management and trust services. SBA lending is one tool it uses for businesses that need longer terms or lower down payments than a conventional loan allows.
sba_fit: Seasonality is the big issue for many Bar Harbor Bank & Trust borrowers. A 7(a) loan with a 10-year term can spread payments out so a summer-heavy hotel or restaurant is not squeezed in the off season, and a 25-year term on real estate helps even more. Buyers of an inn or marina often pair the bank with a 504 loan through a regional CDC. Be ready to show several years of monthly revenue so the lender can see how cash flow moves through the year.

Its roots are in the Rutland area, and it has grown into one of the more visible credit unions in that part of the state.

Most of its members are individuals and families, but it also serves small businesses. Business members tend to be local: contractors, retailers, restaurants, landlords, farms and service companies in Rutland County and nearby central Vermont towns. Business owners usually need to become members before they can borrow. Many of them are sole proprietors or family firms that also keep personal accounts at the credit union.

Credit unions face federal limits on how much business lending they can hold. SBA-guaranteed loans help a credit union like Heritage Family serve business members within those limits, and they let it offer longer terms than its conventional commercial loans. The SBA-guaranteed portion of a loan generally does not count toward that cap, which gives the credit union more room to help local owners grow.
sba_fit: For a Rutland-area owner who already banks with Heritage Family, an SBA 7(a) loan is a way to finance a building, a business purchase or equipment without leaving a familiar institution. Credit union SBA programs are often smaller and more hands-on than a big bank's, so expect personal service but possibly slower turnaround on complex deals. For larger real estate projects, ask whether the credit union works with a Vermont CDC on 504 loans.

sba_fit: Use Arizona Capital Source when your business wants to own its building or buy major equipment and you want a long fixed rate on part of the financing. The 504 debenture portion priced at 6.57% for 25 years in November 2026, which often beats a bank's own fixed rate. You can bring your own bank or ask the CDC for a referral. Your business generally has to occupy at least 51% of an existing building.
